title: Chinese immigrants and Afro-Cubans in Cuban society
summary: Salazar asks about Italians, Chinese, Haitians and Jews; Machito says all discriminated, the Chinese included, and that Chinese were brought in for menial jobs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Okay. I understand that there are different societies there. You say there is from Spain, did they have an Italian community there?
Okay. And which are the ones that discriminated against Afro-Cubans?
All of them, or just some of them?
How , how did the Orientals treat or get along with the Afro-Cuban during that time period?
Let me tell you, they very very discriminatory too.

Yeah, Yeah, because they were pushed around by the whites too; you know that I remember they used to say "Get a Chinese to rent you a room". You understand? It was an insult, so the Chinese when the eh - - - Cuba became republic, nobody want to be a street cleaner, nobody wanted to do this and the other thing so they was bringing Chinese in order to - to ---
In other words, when that happened, the Afro-Cuban was being elevated to a different class?
In a way. The jobs that they gave up were now left to the Orientals?
The Orientals and the Africubans, they used to work in the docks, you know, taking merchandise from the ....
I see, and was that once reserved for whites?
Uhmm - No, the whites they don't, they never--
They never did those menial jobs.
